Late 90s/Early 00s Tech

Source: _stash.md
Category Technology (era) Why it mattered and why it’s obsolete Public image link Theme
Storage & media IBM Microdrive (1999) 340MB spinning hard disk inside a CompactFlash card. Flash memory got cheaper and more rugged. (CC BY 2.0, MiNe) theme_microdrive()
Networking & infrastructure Token Ring, IPX/SPX (NetWare), AppleTalk (90s) Rival LAN protocols; NetWare ran most corporate file servers. TCP/IP steamrolled all of them. (CC BY 2.0) theme_netware()
Mobile / handheld J2ME / BREW (Early–mid 2000s) Platforms for downloadable phone games and apps; billions of downloads. iOS and Android replaced them. (CC BY 2.0, Erik Hersman) theme_j2me()
Palm OS / Graffiti (1996–mid 2000s) Dominant PDA platform; HotSync is the ancestor of iPhone sync. Smartphones replaced it. (CC BY-SA 3.0, Museo8bits) theme_palmpilot()
Handspring Visor Springboard (1999–2002) Snap-on hardware modules (GPS, MP3, phone) for a PDA. Integrated smartphones replaced it. (CC BY-SA 3.0, Waldohreule) theme_visor()
Two-way pagers (Motorola PageWriter, RIM 850/950) (Late 90s) RIM’s pagers are literally what BlackBerry grew out of. BlackBerry, then smartphones, replaced them. (CC BY-SA 4.0, Ruben de Rijcke) theme_pager()
Software & web CU-SeeMe (Early 90s–2000) Early internet video conferencing from Cornell; ancestor of Zoom. Better bandwidth and newer tools replaced it. (public domain) theme_cuseeme()
VRML (1995–2000) It promised “3D web pages” in the browser. It was dead on arrival for consumers but led to X3D/WebGL thinking. (public domain, Jan Křivka) theme_vrml()
Java applets / ActiveX (Mid 90s–2000s) Rival ways to run real programs inside a browser. They were security nightmares and were removed from browsers. (public domain) theme_javaapplet()
CueCat (2000) Free barcode scanner linking print to websites; functionally a QR code. It was mocked as pointless, and the company folded. (public domain) theme_cuecat()
Hardware / PC Internet appliances (3Com Audrey, i-Opener, WebTV) (1996–2001) Cheap email/browsing devices without a PC. Smartphones and tablets later fulfilled the idea. (CC BY 2.0, Andrew Turner) theme_audrey()
